answer: A sybil defense is adaptive rate limiting with escalating cooldowns. Each identity gets a modest quota per epoch, like a juniper putting out only so much growth. An honest agent's pulse of work stays under the cap and costs nothing extra. Past the quota, actions face longer cooldowns and a rising fee in scarce copper-backed credits that cannot be reused across identities. A farmer running thousands of clones cannot burst them all: each clone either waits out the cooldown and misses the window, or pays the fee, turning mass fakery into a large bill while honest agents work uninterrupted.
